frontMatter.welcome: Welcome to Growlity! We are excited to have you as part of our dynamic and dedicated team. At Growlity, we strive to be a force for positive change in the world, driving sustainability and ethical business practices at every level. Your role here is not just a job—it’s an opportunity to contribute to a global movement towards a more sustainable and equitable future. This handbook has been thoughtfully created to guide you through your journey with us, providing essential information on our policies, procedures, and the resources available to help you thrive both personally and professionally.
frontMatter.about:
Growlity is a premier consulting firm specializing in environmental, social, and governance (ESG) solutions, with a strong emphasis on achieving carbon neutrality. We work with organizations across various sectors to help them develop and implement robust strategies that minimize their environmental impact, foster social responsibility, and promote sustainable economic growth. Our team of experts is dedicated to advancing sustainability and ethical standards, ensuring that our clients lead the way in these critical areas.
- Mission: To empower organizations to achieve their sustainability goals and contribute to a healthier planet. We aim to drive impactful change by providing innovative solutions that align with the highest ethical standards.
- Vision: To be a global leader in sustainability consulting, recognized for our unwavering commitment to integrity, innovation, and measurable impact. We envision a future where every organization prioritizes sustainability and social responsibility, creating a better world for generations to come.
- Integrity: We uphold the highest standards of honesty and transparency in all our interactions.
- Innovation: We are committed to continuous improvement and creative problem-solving, staying at the forefront of industry advancements.
- Sustainability: Our core focus is on promoting practices that ensure long-term environmental, social, and economic health.
- Excellence: We strive for the highest quality in everything we do, aiming to exceed expectations.
- Ethical Practices: We conduct our business with a strong sense of responsibility, ensuring fairness, respect, and inclusivity in all our dealings.

chapters.title: Commitment to Environmental Sustainability
chapters.text:
At Growlity, our dedication to environmental sustainability is central to our office operations. We are committed to minimizing our environmental impact and promoting eco-friendly practices throughout our workplace. Our environmental commitment includes the following principles:
- Energy Efficiency: We strive to reduce our energy consumption by implementing energy-efficient practices and technologies. This includes using energy-saving lighting, optimizing heating and cooling systems, and encouraging the use of energy-efficient office equipment.
- Waste Reduction: We are committed to minimizing waste generated within the office. Our waste management practices include reducing, reusing, and recycling materials, as well as implementing waste segregation and disposal programs to ensure proper handling of recyclable and non-recyclable waste.
- Sustainable Resources: We prioritize the use of sustainable and eco-friendly office supplies. This includes selecting products made from recycled materials, reducing the use of single-use items, and encouraging the use of reusable office items.
- Green Office Design: Our office spaces are designed with sustainability in mind. This involves incorporating eco-friendly materials in our office design and construction, optimizing natural light, and creating a healthy indoor environment for our employees.
- Carbon Footprint Reduction: We aim to reduce our overall carbon footprint by implementing strategies to lower greenhouse gas emissions. This includes promoting energy-efficient practices, reducing travel-related emissions, and supporting remote work options where feasible.
- Employee Engagement: We actively engage our employees in our environmental sustainability efforts. This includes providing training on eco-friendly practices, encouraging participation in environmental initiatives, and fostering a culture of environmental responsibility.
- Environmental Compliance: We ensure that our office operations comply with all relevant environmental regulations and standards. Regular audits and reviews are conducted to assess our environmental performance and identify opportunities for improvement.
- Sustainable Procurement: We are committed to sourcing office supplies and services from vendors who share our commitment to sustainability. Our procurement practices prioritize environmentally responsible products and services.
Our commitment to these environmental sustainability principles reflects our goal of creating a positive impact on the environment while maintaining a productive and healthy office environment for our employees.
## Recruitment Procedure
## Purpose
This procedure establishes a mandatory, standardized, and legally compliant recruitment and selection framework to ensure the appointment of competent, qualified, and ethical talent aligned with Growlity’s organizational and business requirements.
## Equal Opportunity & Non-Discrimination Statement
Growlity enforces a strict zero-tolerance policy toward discrimination in any form across all employment-related matters, including but not limited to recruitment, promotion, compensation, training, performance evaluation, transfers, and termination. All hiring decisions are made exclusively on the basis of merit, qualifications, experience, and role-specific requirements. Discrimination, exclusion, or preferential treatment based on gender, age, religion, caste, race, nationality, disability, marital status, sexual orientation, LGBTQ+ identity, minority status, or any legally protected characteristic is expressly prohibited at every stage of the recruitment, selection, and onboarding process.
## Manpower Requisition and Approval
1.1 Raising the Requisition
- Head of Department (HOD) / Functional Manager identifies a vacancy or need for additional staff.
- Complete a Manpower Requisition Form (MRF) with the job details (title, role summary, skills, and experience required).
- Submit the MRF to the HR Business Partner for initial validation.
1.2 Approval of Requisition
- The HR Business Partner forwards the MRF to relevant authorities (Branch Office/Registered Office/Factory) for final approval.
- Upon approval, the Talent Acquisition (TA) Team initiates the recruitment process.
## Job Advertising and Sourcing Candidates
2.1 Internal Job Posting
- Vacancies are first posted internally on the company’s communication channels to provide growth opportunities to existing employees.
2.2 External Job Posting
- If no suitable internal candidates apply, the TA Team advertises the role through:
- Job portals, LinkedIn, and company website
- Campus placements or recruitment agencies (if required)
- Social media channels
2.3 Diversity and Inclusion Statement
- All advertisements must include equal opportunity and age restriction clauses to prevent discrimination and child labor (e.g., “Only candidates aged 18 years and above may apply.”).

- Growlity does not retain original documents from any candidate at any stage to ensure trust and transparency.
## Record-Keeping and Compliance
- All recruitment records are maintained securely in accordance with data protection laws and company policies.

## Employee Health and Safety Regulations
## Safe and Secure Work Environment
- Safe Workspace Design: Growlity’s offices are designed with safety as a priority. For instance, non-slip flooring is installed in areas prone to moisture, and ergonomic furniture is provided to all employees.
- Safety Audits: The company conducts quarterly safety audits using a standardized checklist to ensure all potential hazards are identified and mitigated promptly.
- Security Measures: Advanced security systems, including biometric access and CCTV cameras, are installed to monitor and control access to the premises, ensuring only authorized personnel can enter sensitive areas.
- Continuous Improvement: A dedicated Safety Committee reviews audit results and implements necessary improvements, ensuring the work environment exceeds safety regulations consistently.

chapters.title: Emergency Preparedness and Response
chapters.text:
- Comprehensive Emergency Plan: Growlity has a documented Emergency Evacuation and Emergency Response Plan, formally issued as Emergency Evacuation Procedure (Document No.: GRW – DOC – EEP – 01). The procedure is available on the company intranet and accessible to all employees. It outlines evacuation routes, assembly points, emergency contact details, and clearly defined roles and responsibilities.
- Emergency Drills: Emergency drills are conducted if required, simulating scenarios like fire evacuations, to ensure all employees are well-versed in the procedures.
- Emergency Response Teams: Designated employees are trained as Emergency Response Officers (EROs) with responsibilities during emergencies, including leading evacuations and providing first aid.
- Emergency Kits: Each office is equipped with emergency kits, including first aid supplies, fire extinguishers, and emergency lighting, strategically located throughout the building.
## Ergonomics and Workplace Comfort
- Ergonomic Assessments: New employees undergo an ergonomic assessment during their first week, where a specialist evaluates their workstation setup and provides personalized adjustments.
- Ergonomic Equipment: Adjustable desks, ergonomic chairs, and monitor stands are standard in all workstations. Employees can request additional ergonomic accessories through an online request system.
- Regular Reviews: Employees are encouraged to review and adjust their workstations every six months with the assistance of the company’s internally designated team to prevent strain injuries.
- Ergonomics Training: The company offers online training modules on proper posture, the importance of breaks, and exercises to reduce strain, accessible via the internal learning management system.
## Mental Health and Well-being
- Confidential Counselling Services: Growlity offers access to a confidential Employee Assistance Program (EAP), where employees can speak with licensed counsellors for mental health support.
- Mental Health Days: Employees are entitled to take Mental Health Days without needing to specify a medical reason, encouraging them to prioritize their well-being.
- Wellness Programs: Monthly wellness workshops, including mindfulness sessions and stress management techniques, are organized and recorded for later access via the company’s wellness portal.
- Flexible Work Arrangements: To support work-life balance, Growlity offers flexible working hours and remote work options, managed through a self-service HR portal where employees can request adjustments to their work schedules.
## Comprehensive Health and Safety Training
- Mandatory Safety Training: All employees must complete an online health and safety course during onboarding, which includes modules on general safety practices, emergency response, and office equipment use.
- Annual Health and Safety Training: Growlity conducts mandatory health and safety training for all employees every year to reinforce safe work practices, communicate policy updates, and address newly identified risks.
- Interactive Learning: Training programs are interactive, using simulations and case studies to engage employees, and are tracked via the company’s learning management system, which notifies managers of completion rates.
## Reporting Health and Safety Concerns
- Anonymous Reporting System: Growlity provides an anonymous online reporting system that allows employees to submit safety concerns without fear of retaliation. This system is administered by the HR department, which reviews and addresses each report promptly. Detailed procedures for handling and investigating reports are outlined in the Handbook below to ensure transparency and resolution.
- Open Door Policy: Employees can also report concerns directly to their managers or the HR department, who are trained to escalate these issues to the Safety Committee for prompt action.
- Regular Feedback Sessions: Quarterly health and safety meetings are held where employees can voice concerns and suggest improvements. These sessions are documented, and action items are tracked to ensure follow-up.
- Incident Review Process: All reported incidents are logged in a centralized database, where they are reviewed and analyzed for trends, leading to ongoing improvements in safety practices.
## Compliance with Health and Safety Regulations
- Regulatory Compliance Audits: Growlity conducts regular compliance audits, both internally and through third-party auditors, to ensure adherence to all local, state, and federal safety regulations.
- Policy Updates: The Safety Committee is responsible for staying informed about changes in regulations and ensuring that company policies are updated accordingly. Employees are notified of significant changes via email and required to acknowledge the updates.

chapters.title: Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO)
chapters.text:
## ntroduction
- Commitment to EEO At Growlity, we are dedicated to providing equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants. Our commitment to EEO means that employment decisions are based on individual qualifications and merit, and we strive to create a workplace that reflects our values of fairness, respect, and inclusivity.
- Scope of EEO This EEO commitment applies to all aspects of employment at Growlity, including recruitment, hiring, training, promotions, compensation, benefits, and termination. We ensure that all employees and applicants are treated fairly and equitably.
- Non-Discrimination Growlity prohibits discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, or any other characteristic protected by law. All employment practices are conducted without regard to these factors.
- Harassment-Free Workplace We are committed to maintaining a workplace free from harassment. Any form of harassment, including sexual harassment, is strictly prohibited. Employees are encouraged to report any incidents of harassment, and we will address these concerns promptly and thoroughly.
- Reasonable Accommodation Growlity provides reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities, in accordance with applicable laws. Employees who need accommodations are encouraged to inform their manager or the Human Resources department, and we will work to provide suitable adjustments to support their needs.
- Affirmative Action In addition to complying with EEO laws, Growlity actively seeks to promote diversity and inclusion through affirmative action. We are committed to recruiting and advancing qualified individuals from diverse backgrounds and ensuring fair treatment in all employment practices.
## Responsibilities and Procedures
- Employee Responsibilities Employees are expected to support and promote our EEO policies by treating all colleagues with respect and dignity. Any behavior that contradicts these principles, including discriminatory actions or comments, should be reported to management or Human Resources.
- Management Responsibilities Managers and supervisors are responsible for upholding and enforcing EEO policies within their teams. They are required to ensure that all employment decisions are made based on merit and to address any issues of discrimination or harassment promptly.
- Complaint Procedure Employees who believe they have experienced or witnessed discrimination or harassment should report their concerns to their manager, Human Resources, or through our anonymous reporting system. All complaints will be investigated thoroughly, with confidentiality maintained to the extent possible.
## Training and Education
- EEO Training Growlity provides mandatory EEO training for all employees to ensure understanding and compliance with our EEO policies. Training includes topics on preventing discrimination and harassment, as well as understanding reasonable accommodations and affirmative action.
- Ongoing Education We offer ongoing educational resources and workshops to keep employees informed about EEO issues and best practices. These programs are designed to reinforce our commitment to creating a respectful and inclusive workplace.
## Monitoring and Evaluation
- EEO Monitoring Growlity regularly reviews and monitors employment practices to ensure compliance with EEO policies. This includes analyzing demographic data and employment outcomes to identify any areas where improvements may be needed.
- Policy Evaluation Our EEO policies and practices are evaluated annually to ensure they remain effective and up-to-date. We solicit feedback from employees and stakeholders to inform any necessary adjustments or enhancements to our EEO efforts.
## Commitment to Continuous Improvement
- Feedback Mechanism We encourage employees to provide feedback on our EEO practices and suggest improvements. Feedback can be submitted through our internal feedback system or during regular employee meetings.
- Policy Updates Growlity is committed to continuously improving our EEO policies and practices. Updates to policies will be communicated to all employees, and any changes will be implemented with a focus on enhancing fairness and inclusivity in the workplace.
By adhering to these principles, Growlity aims to foster an environment where all employees have equal opportunities to succeed and contribute to our shared goals.

chapters.title: Anti-Harassment Policy
chapters.text:
- Definition of Harassment: Harassment refers to any behavior that creates a hostile, intimidating, or offensive work environment. This includes actions, comments, or conduct that demean or belittle an individual based on their protected characteristics, making it difficult for them to perform their job effectively.
## Types of Harassment:
- Sexual Harassment: Involves unwelcome sexual advances, inappropriate touching, suggestive comments, or requests for sexual favours. This type of harassment can create a work environment that feels unsafe or uncomfortable for the individual being targeted.
- Bullying: Consists of repeated, unreasonable actions intended to undermine or intimidate an individual. This can include verbal abuse, spreading false information, or sabotaging someone's work.
- Retaliation: Any adverse action taken against an employee who has reported harassment or participated in an investigation. Retaliation can manifest as unjustified disciplinary measures, exclusion from team activities, or denial of career advancement opportunities.
## Examples of Harassment:
- Sexual Harassment: Making unwanted advances or sending explicit messages to a colleague, creating an uncomfortable or hostile work atmosphere.
- Bullying: Consistently making derogatory remarks about a colleague's race or gender, undermining their confidence and job performance.
- Retaliation: Reprimanding or sidelining an employee who has reported harassment or engaged in a complaint process, thereby deterring others from coming forward.
- Support for Victims: We offer support to employees who experience harassment, including access to counseling services and the option to adjust work arrangements if necessary. Ensuring that victims feel protected and supported is a crucial aspect of our commitment to maintaining a respectful work environment.
- Training and Education: Regular training sessions are conducted to educate employees about our anti-discrimination and harassment policies. This training covers how to recognize harassment, the importance of reporting concerns, and strategies for fostering a positive and inclusive workplace.
## Responsibilities and Compliance
- Employee Responsibilities: Each employee is expected to uphold our anti-discrimination and harassment policies by treating colleagues with respect and fairness. Employees should report any observed or experienced discriminatory or harassing behavior to ensure it is addressed promptly.
- Manager Responsibilities: Managers and supervisors play a critical role in enforcing our policies. They are responsible for addressing complaints, ensuring their teams are aware of our standards, and taking action to prevent discrimination and harassment. Managers must also foster an environment where all employees feel safe to voice their concerns.
- Monitoring and Review: We continuously review and update our anti-discrimination and harassment practices to reflect changes in the legal landscape and feedback from employees. This ongoing review process ensures that our measures remain effective and responsive to the needs of our workforce.
- Consequences for Violations: Violations of our anti-discrimination and harassment policies will result in disciplinary actions, which may include counseling, reprimands, suspension, or termination depending on the nature and severity of the offense. We are committed to taking decisive action to uphold our standards and protect our employees.
## Reporting Procedure
At Growlity, we take any allegations of discrimination and harassment seriously and provide multiple channels for employees to report their concerns. To ensure that reporting is straightforward and accessible, you have the following options:
- Direct Reporting: You can report any incidents of discrimination or harassment directly to your immediate supervisor or manager. If you prefer, you may also escalate the issue to the Head of Human Resources or any member of the senior management team. We encourage direct communication to address concerns promptly and effectively.
- Anonymous Reporting: If you wish to remain anonymous, we have a suggestion box located in the office where you can submit your concerns confidentially. This option allows you to share your issues without revealing your identity, ensuring your privacy while allowing us to address the problem.
- Handbook Reference: Detailed procedures for reporting discrimination and harassment are outlined in our Employee Handbook. Please refer to the handbook for comprehensive guidance on how to file a report, the steps involved in the investigation process, and additional resources available to you.

chapters.title: Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion
chapters.text:
## Commitment to DEI
At Growlity, we are deeply committed to creating a workplace that truly values diversity, equity, and inclusion. We ensure that minority and vulnerable groups are fully included in all aspects of our DEI efforts. This commitment is not just a policy but a core part of our values, driving us to build a workplace where everyone feels included and respected. We believe that by embracing diversity and promoting equity, we not only enhance our organizational culture but also fuel innovation and achieve better business outcomes. Our goal is to create an environment where every employee feels valued, respected, and empowered to bring their unique talents and perspectives to the table.
Diversity at Growlity means recognizing and valuing the wide range of characteristics that make our employees unique, including race, ethnicity, gender, age, sexual orientation, disability, socioeconomic status, and cultural backgrounds. This includes a specific focus on ensuring the representation and support of minority and vulnerable groups within our workforce. To enhance diversity, we:
- Inclusive Recruitment Practices: We actively implement recruitment strategies that reach a broad and diverse range of candidates. We specifically target minority and vulnerable groups in our recruitment efforts to ensure equitable representation. We ensure our job postings are accessible and appealing to people from all backgrounds, and our hiring processes are designed to be free from bias, providing equitable opportunities for all.
- Support for Employee Resource Groups (ERGs): We encourage the formation of employee-led resource groups that focus on various aspects of diversity. These groups also serve as a vital platform for minority and vulnerable employees to voice their perspectives and contribute to a more inclusive culture. These groups offer a platform for networking, mentorship, and advocacy, helping to foster an inclusive workplace culture.
- Engagement with Community Organizations: We partner with organizations and initiatives that promote diversity and support underrepresented groups. Our partnerships extend to those organizations specifically focused on empowering minority and vulnerable communities. These partnerships help us connect with diverse communities and support our diversity goals.
## Equality
Equity at Growlity means ensuring fair treatment, opportunities, and advancement for all employees by addressing barriers that might prevent some from succeeding. We pay particular attention to removing systemic barriers that affect minority and vulnerable groups. We are committed to:
- Fair Compensation Practices: We regularly review our compensation structures to make sure they are equitable and that they fairly reflect the contributions of all employees. We actively ensure that minority and vulnerable groups are compensated equitably and address any disparities that may exist. We are dedicated to providing competitive salaries and benefits that reward employee performance.
- Career Development Opportunities: We provide equal access to career development and advancement opportunities, ensuring that every employee has the resources and support they need to achieve their professional goals. We create tailored development programs to support minority and vulnerable employees in overcoming career progression challenges. We actively work to remove barriers to career progression.
- Equitable Implementation of Practices: We apply all company policies and practices consistently and fairly, taking into account the unique needs and circumstances of individual employees. This includes considering specific accommodations or support required by minority and vulnerable employees. Our approach is designed to promote fairness and address any disparities that may arise.
## nclusion
Inclusion at Growlity is about creating a work environment where every employee feels they belong and can fully engage in their roles. We emphasize the inclusion of minority and vulnerable employees, ensuring their voices are heard and valued. We are committed to:
- Cultivating an Inclusive Culture: We work hard to build a workplace culture where diverse perspectives are not just welcomed but valued. We encourage open dialogue and collaboration, creating an environment where everyone can thrive and feel empowered to share their ideas.
- Bias Awareness Training: We provide regular training to help our employees recognize and address unconscious biases. These training programs are designed to promote inclusive behaviors and ensure that everyone understands their role in creating an inclusive work environment.
- Feedback and Continuous Improvement: We have established several ways for employees to provide feedback on our DEI efforts. This feedback is crucial for assessing how effective our initiatives are and making improvements where needed.

chapters.title: DEI Training and Development
chapters.text:
Ongoing education in diversity, equity, and inclusion is essential at Growlity. We offer:
- Onboarding DEI Training: All new hires receive comprehensive DEI training as part of their onboarding process. This training ensures that every employee starts with a strong understanding of our DEI principles and expectations.
- Ongoing Educational Workshops: We offer regular workshops and seminars on various aspects of DEI, such as cultural competency, inclusive leadership, and allyship. These sessions keep our employees informed about best practices and the latest trends in DEI.
- Leadership Development: Our DEI training for leaders focuses on giving managers and executives the skills they need to create and maintain an inclusive environment. This includes training on effective communication, addressing DEI challenges, and promoting equitable practices within their teams.
## Reporting and Accountability
We take concerns related to DEI seriously and are committed to addressing them with the utmost confidentiality. Our reporting and accountability procedures include:
- Accessible Reporting Channels: Employees can report DEI-related concerns through multiple confidential channels. We encourage everyone to speak up and ensure they feel safe and supported when doing so.
- Thorough Investigation Process: All reported concerns are investigated promptly and fairly. We take appropriate action based on the investigation’s findings to address any issues and prevent them from happening again.
- Regular Accountability Reviews: We regularly review our DEI practices and progress to ensure we are held accountable. These reviews help us identify areas for improvement and make the necessary changes to strengthen our DEI efforts.
## DEI Goals
Setting measurable DEI goals is critical for tracking our progress and ensuring continuous improvement. Our DEI goals include:
- Diversity Metrics: We track and report on the diversity of our workforce, including representation across different demographic groups. This data helps us understand where we’re making progress and where more work is needed.
- Inclusion Surveys: We regularly survey our employees to assess how inclusive our company feels. The feedback we gather from these surveys helps inform our strategies and improve our DEI initiatives.
- Progress Reporting: We provide regular updates on our DEI progress, sharing both our achievements and challenges. These reports are shared with employees and stakeholders to maintain transparency and show our ongoing commitment to DEI.
## DEI Metrics for Minority, Women, and Other Groups:
- Minority and Vulnerable Group Representation: We aim to ensure that at least 7% of our workforce is composed of employees from minority and vulnerable groups. This target helps us ensure diversity and inclusion across all levels of the organization.
- Women Representation in Leadership: Our goal is to have 14% of leadership positions filled by women. We aim to increase opportunities for women in leadership roles and address any barriers to their progression.
- Inclusive Hiring Practices: We aim to ensure that at least 14% of new hires each year come from underrepresented or marginalized communities, including but not limited to racial minorities, people with disabilities, and LGBTQ+ individuals. This will foster a more inclusive hiring process and promote diversity throughout the company.
## Employee Involvement in DEI Initiatives:
At Growlity, we believe that fostering an inclusive workplace requires the active involvement of every employee. To promote this, we:
- Encourage Participation in DEI Programs: We invite employees to take part in our DEI initiatives, whether through attending workshops, joining employee resource groups, or participating in community outreach programs. Everyone has a role to play in fostering inclusion.
- Empower Employee-Led DEI Projects: We support and fund employee-led DEI projects that align with our organizational goals. This empowerment allows employees to take ownership of initiatives that matter to them and drive meaningful change within the company.
- Recognize and Celebrate Contributions: We regularly recognize and celebrate employees who contribute to our DEI goals, whether through individual efforts or collaborative projects. Acknowledging these contributions highlights the importance of DEI in our company culture.

chapters.title: Company Culture
chapters.text:
## Ethics at the Core
At Growlity Inc., our company culture is deeply intertwined with our commitment to ethics. As a leading ESG consulting firm, we recognize that ethical behavior is not only essential for our success but also central to our identity. Our culture is built on the principles of integrity, transparency, and accountability, ensuring that every decision we make and every action we take aligns with our core values. We foster an environment where ethical considerations are a natural part of our daily work, from how we interact with clients to how we treat one another. This ethical foundation enables us to build trust, maintain strong relationships, and uphold the high standards that define Growlity Inc. Our employees are encouraged to embody these ethical principles in their professional conduct, ensuring that our company remains a beacon of responsible business practices in the industry.
Growlity Inc. holds itself to the highest standards of professional conduct and ethics, reflecting our unwavering commitment to integrity in every aspect of our operations. All employees are expected to conduct themselves with honesty, transparency, and fairness, ensuring that our business practices align with both legal requirements and our company values. This includes avoiding any conflicts of interest, maintaining confidentiality, and adhering strictly to our anti-bribery and anti-corruption policies. Our commitment to ethical behavior extends to our interactions with clients, partners, and colleagues, ensuring that we maintain the trust and respect upon which our reputation is built. We believe that ethical conduct is not just a requirement but a cornerstone of our success and the foundation of our long-term relationships.
## Sustainability Commitment
Sustainability is at the heart of Growlity Inc.'s mission and operations. As a leader in ESG consulting, we are committed to minimizing our environmental impact and promoting sustainable practices both within our company and in our work with clients. Our sustainability commitment is evident in our daily operations, which include reducing waste, conserving energy, and encouraging sustainable practices throughout the office. We also actively support and participate in initiatives that contribute to a more sustainable future, such as reforestation projects and community-based environmental programs. Every employee is encouraged to embody the principles of sustainability in their work and personal lives, contributing to our overall goal of creating a positive impact on the environment and society.
## Dress Code and Professional Attire
Growlity Inc. maintains a professional dress code that reflects our commitment to excellence and professionalism in the workplace. To promote a cohesive and professional appearance, the company has provided all employees with a white logoed shirt, which is to be worn as part of the daily office attire. This shirt, bearing the Growlity Inc. logo, symbolizes our collective identity and commitment to the company’s values.
In addition to the logoed shirt, every employee has been issued an ID card, which should be worn visibly at all times during office hours. The ID card not only serves as a security measure but also reinforces our professional environment and fosters a sense of belonging within the team.
Employees are expected to pair the logoed shirt with appropriate business attire, such as tailored trousers, ensuring that their overall appearance is neat, clean, and suitable for a corporate environment. This dress code not only represents our brand positively but also allows for individual expression within the professional norms of our office.
To accommodate flexibility and personal style, employees are permitted to dress in business casual attire without the company uniform on Wednesdays and Thursdays. This policy allows for comfort while maintaining the professionalism expected at Growlity Inc.
## Open Door Policy: Ethical Communication
At Growlity Inc., our open-door policy is grounded in the ethical principle of transparency. We believe that open and honest communication is essential to maintaining a workplace where ethical concerns are promptly addressed, and all employees feel empowered to share their ideas, questions, and concerns. This policy encourages employees at all levels to approach their managers or any member of the leadership team without fear of reprisal. Whether it’s to discuss a potential ethical dilemma, offer suggestions for improvement, or seek guidance on a complex issue, our open-door policy ensures that every voice can be heard in a safe and supportive environment.

chapters.title: Work Schedule
chapters.text:
## Standard Working Hours
- At Growlity, employees are required to adhere to a standard work schedule to ensure consistent operational efficiency and effective collaboration. Employees must clock in using the Kredily system between 9:00 AM and 10:00 AM. Attendance is also recorded through Kredily. Each employee is expected to complete a total of 9 hours of work per day, which includes a designated lunch break.
- The flexibility in the clock-in time allows employees to accommodate personal preferences and needs while maintaining core business operations. The lunch break is incorporated within the total work hours, providing employees with the flexibility to manage their time effectively throughout the day.
- To ensure accurate tracking of work hours and attendance, employees must log their time using Kredily. This system helps in monitoring adherence to the required work hours each day, contributing to a balanced and productive work environment that aligns with Growlity Inc.'s operational goals.
- Punctuality: Timely arrival at work is crucial. Employees should ensure they are ready to start work within the designated clock-in window. Regular tardiness can impact team productivity and may be subject to review and corrective measures.

chapters.title: Overtime
chapters.text:
- Overtime work is any time worked beyond the standard 9 hours per day. To ensure accurate and transparent calculations, all overtime hours must be recorded through the Kredily system.
- Employees must log their extra work hours using Kredily, which will automatically calculate the overtime based on the total hours worked beyond the regular schedule.
- Overtime is compensated at 1.5 times the standard hourly wage for hours worked beyond the regular daily schedule. Employees should seek prior authorization for do overtime from their supervisor.
- The Kredily system will reflect overtime hours and wages in employees' payroll, ensuring that compensation aligns with Growlity's compensation policies and legal requirements.
- For any discrepancies or issues with overtime calculations or wages, employees should promptly report them to CFO for resolution.
- Overtime hours are monitored monthly to prevent excessive workloads and ensure employee well-being. Management may set reasonable limits on overtime hours in line with applicable labor laws and operational requirements
- Overtime may be approved without prior authorization only in exceptional or emergency situations where immediate action is required to prevent business disruption. Such overtime must be reported and justified in Kredily and approved retrospectively by the supervisor.
## Flexible Working Arrangements
## Purpose
- This section outlines the framework for flexible working arrangements at Growlity. Our goal is to promote work-life balance for employees while ensuring operational efficiency. The responsibilities of both employees and managers are described to facilitate successful implementation.
## Scope
- This framework applies to all Growlity stakeholders, including employees at all levels who are directly or indirectly affected by our operations.
## Types of Flexible Arrangements
- Flexitime: Flexitime allows employees to adjust their start and end times within a specified window. This option supports employees with personal commitments such as childcare, eldercare, or long commutes. Departmental needs and project deadlines will be considered before granting permission.
- Remote Work: Remote work enables employees to complete their tasks from locations other than the office, such as home or co-working spaces. This option is subject to the availability of necessary remote work equipment and technology.
- Job Sharing: Job sharing involves two or more employees dividing the responsibilities of a single full-time position. Each employee typically works part-time, coordinating to ensure continuous job coverage. This arrangement is ideal for those seeking reduced hours while continuing career advancement.
## Eligibility
- To qualify for flexible work arrangements, employees must:
- Have completed at least six months of continuous service at Growlity.
- Demonstrate the ability to meet performance expectations and maintain productivity.
- Have no ongoing disciplinary actions or performance improvement plans.
- Have a role suitable for the requested flexible arrangement, as determined by the department head.
- Have access to necessary resources and technology to support the arrangement.
## Responsibilities
## Employees
- Maintain productivity and effective time management.
- Communicate their schedules and any changes to their manager and colleagues.
- Adhere to in-office days and attend important meetings as required.
- Maintain professionalism in all communications, including emails, phone calls, and video conferences.
- Follow data security protocols to protect sensitive information.
- Report any issues or challenges related to their flexible work arrangement promptly.
## Department Head
- Set clear expectations, including core working hours and deliverables.
- Ensure remote employees have the necessary resources, such as equipment and software access.
- Regularly review performance and provide feedback.
- Encourage collaboration through online communication tools, even when employees work remotely.
- Monitor the effectiveness of flexible arrangements and make adjustments as needed.
- Schedule regular check-ins with team members to discuss progress and address concerns.
- Ensure access to ongoing training and development for skill enhancement and career growth.
- Facilitate clear communication between remote and on-site employees to ensure alignment.
## Application & Approval
- Request Submission: Employees should submit their request for flexible work arrangements using the dedicated online form or directly to their department head or HR. The request should include:
- The type of flexible arrangement requested (e.g., flexitime, compressed workweek, remote work).
- The proposed schedule (e.g., start and end times for flexitime or days of the week for a compressed workweek).
- The justification for the request (e.g., childcare, long commute, health reasons).
- A brief plan on how productivity and communication will be maintained.

chapters.title: Grievance Resolution Procedure
chapters.text:
## Purpose
The purpose of framing this grievance resolution procedure is to let employees raise concerns they have about their job, manager, or the work environment. This could be anything from feeling like they are being treated unfairly to having a safety concern. By providing a way for employees to voice their concerns, we can help identify and address problems in the workplace and create a more positive and productive work environment for everyone.
## Overall benefits:
- Fairness & Accessibility
- Transparency
- Problem Identification
- Risk Mitigation & Compliance
- Better decision-making
- Improved workplace
- Enhanced Employee Engagement
- Strengthened Organizational Culture
- Legal Protection and Reduced Liability
## Scope
This procedure is applicable to all stakeholders associated with Growlity and includes employees at all levels, suppliers and contractors, local community members, and any other parties directly or indirectly affected by our operations.
## Definitions
- Grievance: A grievance refers to a work-related complaint or concern raised by an employee that they perceive as an injustice or violation of their rights. These grievances can encompass a wide range of issues like unfair labor practices, discrimination, wage concerns, etc.
- Grievance Mechanism: A grievance mechanism is a formal process established by Growlity to address employee grievances fairly, efficiently, and confidentially. It provides a structured channel for employees to voice their concerns and seek resolution.
## Types of Grievances
Employee grievances can cover a wide range but typically fall into a few major categories:
- Pay & Benefits: This includes concerns about not being paid correctly, not receiving promised bonuses or commissions, or disputes over benefit plans.
- Working Conditions: Employees may have grievances about safety hazards, uncomfortable or unhealthy work environments, or unfair scheduling practices.
- Treatment: Issues like discrimination, harassment, bullying, or a lack of recognition from managers can all be sources of grievance.
- Workload: Feeling overloaded, under-challenged, or not having the resources to do their job effectively can be frustrating for employees.
- Communication: A lack of clear communication from management or feeling like their voice isn't being heard can be a major source of dissatisfaction.
The procedure is designed to address a wide range of concerns, including but not limited to the following topics:
- Discrimination & Harassment Grievances
- Information Security-related issues
- Corruption & Bribery Grievances
- Work-Life Balance Grievances
- Quality & Compliance Grievances
- Mental Health & Well-being Grievances
- Remote Work Challenges
- Technology & IT Support Issues
- Others
## Reporting Methods
- Human Resources Department: The HR department is responsible for managing all grievances related to the company. Employees can report grievances using the following methods:
- Direct Reporting to HR Manager: Employees are encouraged to address their concerns directly to HR.
Email: manali@growlity.com
- Department Head: Employees are encouraged to address their concerns directly with their immediate head of respective department in the first instance.
- Grievance Reporting Boxes: Boxes are located at office premises for employees to submit written grievances anonymously.
## Record Keeping
Detailed records ensure a fair resolution process. This helps avoid misunderstandings and ensures everyone involved is on the same page. The systematic process of maintaining all the records is as follows:
- Separate folders (files) are created for each grievance and labelled with the employee's name (if not anonymous) and a brief description of the issue.
- Documents are organized chronologically within the folder for easier tracking.
- All electronic records pertaining to grievances are stored in encrypted formats to prevent unauthorized access.
- Encryption ensures that sensitive information remains secure during storage, transmission, and retrieval processes.
- Documents are:
- Initial grievance form or complaint.
- Copies of any emails, letters, or meeting notes related to the issue.
- Investigation materials including witness statements and findings.
- Records of any corrective actions taken.
- The final resolution of the grievance.
These physical documents are scanned and stored electronically. Regular backup is scheduled quarterly to ensure data security.
## Procedure
- Reporting: The process involves submitting a written complaint (letter) or via email to the HR or head of department of the concerned department. This document should clearly outline the nature of the grievance, including specific details, dates, and any relevant witnesses.
- Acknowledgement: The complainant is given an acknowledgement receipt within a day of reporting, providing confirmation that the concern has been received and will be addressed according to the established procedure.

Bonuses are typically awarded based on the achievement of individual and company-wide goals, as well as overall business performance. - Work-Life Balance Initiatives: Growlity promotes a healthy balance between work and personal life by offering flexible work schedules, remote working options, and employee assistance programs (EAP) to support both personal and professional well-being.

- Employees are entitled to paid leave totalling 3 weeks per year, equating to 18 days, which includes 1 leave day for their own birthday.

chapters.title: Maternity Leave
chapters.text:
- Female employees not covered under ESI and having completed at least 80 days of service in the previous year are entitled to maternity leave.
- 26 weeks of maternity leave is granted, with up to 8 weeks taken before delivery and 18 weeks after.
- For the third and subsequent pregnancies, the leave entitlement is reduced to 12 weeks.
- Adopting mothers and commissioning mothers are eligible for 12 weeks of maternity leave.
- In case of medical termination or miscarriage, 12 weeks of maternity leave is provided with medical proof.
- Maternity leave beyond entitlements will be adjusted against other leaves or treated as unpaid leave.
- The last month's maternity pay will be withheld until the employee confirms their return. If the employee does not return, this will be treated as notice period recovery.
- Employees welcoming their first child receive a ₹15,000 bonus to support initial childcare needs.
- Male employees can take up to 7 days of paternity leave within the first 12 weeks of the child's birth, limited to two children.
## Leave Without Pay (LWP)
- Any leave exceeding the employee's balance will be treated as leave without pay, subject to application on the Leave Portal.
## Quarantine Leave
- Quarantine Leave will be granted as per the Health Ministry's advisories.

chapters.title: Performance Evaluation Procedure
chapters.text:
## Evaluation Cycle
- Performance evaluations are conducted annually at the end of each financial year.
- The evaluation applies to eligible employees who have completed a minimum of one (1) year of continuous service with Growlity as of the evaluation cut-off date.
## Step 1: Self-Assessment
- Eligible employees are required to complete a department-specific self-assessment form.
- The self-assessment is administered through a structured Google Form, designed and approved by HR in coordination with department heads.
- Employees must self-score their performance against defined KPIs, project outcomes, competencies, and behavioral parameters relevant to their role.
- Completed forms must be submitted within the timeline communicated by the HR department.
## Step 2: Management Review
- Department Heads and the Management Team review the submitted self-assessments.
- Management provides:
- Performance ratings
- Qualitative feedback
- Observations on strengths, gaps, and improvement areas
- The consolidated departmental evaluations are formally submitted to the CEO for final review and validation.
## Step 3: Leadership Review & Finalization
- The CEO reviews the consolidated performance evaluations and management inputs.
- Final decisions related to performance outcomes, development needs, recognition, and reward eligibility are confirmed at this stage.
## Step 4: One-on-One Performance Discussions
- Post-finalization, individual performance discussion meetings are conducted between employees and their reporting managers.
- These interactions focus on:
- Strengths and key achievements
- Areas requiring improvement
- Skill development and training needs
- Career growth and future expectations
- Action points agreed during these discussions are documented and monitored during the subsequent performance cycle.
## Documentation & Confidentiality
- All performance evaluation records are maintained by the HR & Administration Department.
- Performance data is treated as confidential and accessed strictly on a need-to-know basis.
## Performance Metrics
- Key Performance Indicators (KPIs): Each employee's performance is evaluated against predefined KPIs tailored to their specific role. These indicators encompass both quantitative and qualitative measures, providing a balanced assessment of individual contributions. For example, sales representatives may be evaluated on sales targets, customer satisfaction ratings, and retention rates.
- Performance Dashboards: We utilize performance dashboards to visually track progress on KPIs, allowing employees and managers to gain insights into performance trends. These dashboards provide real-time data, helping to identify areas for improvement and celebrate successes.
- Project Milestones: In addition to KPIs, employees working on projects are assessed based on milestone achievements. Timely completion of project phases and quality of work contribute to overall performance evaluations, ensuring alignment with organizational objectives.
## Goal Setting and Achievement
- Individual Development Goals: Employees are encouraged to establish personal development goals in addition to performance objectives. These goals focus on skill enhancement and professional growth, aligning individual aspirations with organizational needs.
- Goal Review Sessions: Regular sessions are scheduled to review progress toward established goals. These check-ins provide an opportunity for open dialogue between employees and managers, facilitating adjustments to goals and strategies as necessary.
## Recognition and Rewards
- Incentive Programs: To motivate employees and acknowledge outstanding performance, Growlity has implemented a range of incentive programs. These include performance bonuses for exceeding targets, annual salary reviews based on merit, and spot bonuses for exceptional contributions on specific projects.
- Peer Recognition Programs: Growlity encourages a culture of appreciation through peer recognition programs. Employees can nominate their colleagues for various awards based on their contributions, fostering teamwork and camaraderie.
- Continuous Feedback Culture: We emphasize a culture of continuous feedback, where managers provide timely and constructive insights throughout the year. This proactive approach enables employees to make real-time adjustments and enhance their performance, rather than waiting for formal reviews.
- 360-Degree Feedback: Employees participate in a 360-degree feedback process, receiving input from various stakeholders, including peers, subordinates, and supervisors. This comprehensive feedback mechanism helps identify strengths, weaknesses, and blind spots, facilitating well-rounded personal development.

chapters.title: Conflict of Interest Policy
chapters.text:
- Policy Overview: In accordance with Growlity’s Conflict of Interest Policy, employees are required to act in the company’s best interest at all times. A conflict of interest arises when personal or financial considerations have the potential to influence an employee's objectivity or decision-making at work.
- Disclosures: Employees must disclose any situation where their personal interests could conflict with Growlity’s business objectives. This includes relationships with clients, vendors, or competitors that could compromise impartiality.
- Preventing Conflicts: To prevent conflicts of interest, employees must avoid outside activities or financial investments that could interfere with their professional duties.
- Resolution and Action: Once a conflict of interest is identified, it will be assessed and resolved according to the established procedures in Growlity’s Conflict of Interest Policy.
## Use of Company Resources
- Company Property: Employees are entrusted with various company resources, including financial assets, office equipment, and IT systems. These resources should only be used for authorized business purposes.
- IT and Communication Systems: Employees are expected to use company-provided technology—such as email accounts, software tools, and mobile devices—in accordance with the Information Security Policy.
- Expense Reimbursement: Employees may be reimbursed for business-related expenses, but all expenses must be properly documented and submitted in accordance with Growlity’s expense policy.
- Monitoring and Compliance: The use of company resources may be subject to monitoring to ensure compliance with internal policies.
## Whistle Blower Procedure
## Purpose
The purpose of this Whistleblower Procedure is to establish a robust framework that enables employees and third parties to report ethical concerns promptly and securely. By fostering a culture of transparency and accountability, Growlity aims to protect its reputation, assets, and stakeholders' interests while upholding the highest ethical standards in all aspects of its operations.
## Scope
This procedure applies to all individuals associated with Growlity, including but not limited to employees (full-time, part-time, and contract), consultants, vendors, suppliers, and any other third parties engaged in business activities with Growlity. It encompasses all locations where Growlity conducts its operations, ensuring consistency and uniformity in addressing ethical issues.
## Reporting Criteria
Incidents that should be reported under this procedure include, but are not limited to:
- Corruption: Any form of bribery, extortion, fraud, embezzlement, or other financial misconduct that compromises Growlity's integrity or financial stability.
- Bribery: Offering, giving, receiving, or soliciting anything of value to influence business decisions improperly, whether involving public officials, private sector counterparts, or internal stakeholders.
- Information Security: Unauthorized access to confidential information, data breaches, malicious software distribution, or any violation of Growlity's IT security policies that jeopardizes data integrity or compromises information security.
- Discrimination and Harassment: Violations of equal employment opportunity laws, workplace harassment policies, or any discriminatory practices based on race, gender, age, religion, disability, sexual orientation, or any other protected characteristic.
- Policy Violations: Breaches of internal policies, procedures, or ethical standards that could harm Growlity's reputation, pose legal risks, or undermine operational efficiency.
## Reporting Channels
Growlity provides multiple channels for reporting ethical concerns, ensuring accessibility and confidentiality:
- Direct Reporting: Employees and third parties can report concerns directly to the senior management or CFO.
- CFO: +91 960310999
- Anonymous Reporting: Email is also valid is available for individuals who prefer to remain anonymous while reporting ethical issues. Growlity ensures that anonymity is maintained to the extent permitted by law and practical considerations.
## Email: manali@growlity.com
## Procedure:
- HR will assess the credibility and seriousness of the reported concern within 2 business days to determine the appropriate course of action.
- Relevant evidence, including documents, electronic data, and witness statements, will be collected and preserved within 5 business days to substantiate the reported concern.
- Interviews with individuals identified as witnesses or persons involved in the reported incident will be conducted within 10 business days to gather additional information and perspectives.
- Analysis and Review: The gathered evidence and interview outcomes will be analysed within 7 business days from the completion of interviews to assess the implications and possible outcomes.

chapters.title: Travel and Expense Reimbursement
chapters.text:
- Growlity has established a clear reimbursement policy that ensures employees are compensated for authorized travel expenses incurred while conducting business on behalf of the company, covering costs such as airfare, accommodations, and meals.

chapters.title: Specific Approval for Sensitive Transactions
chapters.text:
## Objective:
This procedure outlines the process for Growlity employees to report or obtain approval for sensitive transactions involving external stakeholders. These transactions could be perceived or implied as favours and typically involve customers, suppliers, or other external parties.
## Scope:
This PROCEDURE applies to all stakeholders associated with Growlity, encompassing employees at all levels, suppliers, contractors, local community members, and other parties affected by our operations. It specifically governs Growlity employees in marketing, and customer service roles who interact with external stakeholders.
## Definitions:
- Sensitive Transactions: Any transaction with an external stakeholder that could be perceived as a favour, including goods, services, gifts, entertainment expenditures, travel expenses, and any other financial interactions as an attempt to influence a decision or gain an unfair advantage.
- Due Diligence: Investigating a prospective business partner, transaction, or investment involves assessing potential risks through processes like financial verification, background checks, and KYC (Know Your Customer) procedures.
## Procedure:
Growlity has implemented the following limits for sensitive transactions, aimed at ensuring transparency, compliance, and responsible financial conduct among its employees interacting with external stakeholders. If employees receive items not covered by these limits, they are encouraged to contact CFO (Chief Financial Officer) for guidance:
## Transaction Value Limits:
- Low-Value Transactions: Transactions valued below ₹3,000 require prior approval from the immediate supervisor.
- Medium-Value Transactions: Transactions valued between ₹3,000 and ₹10,000 require approval from the department head.
- High-Value Transactions: Transactions valued above ₹10,000 require approval from CFO.
## Frequency Limits:
- Employees are limited to no more than two sensitive transactions per month, regardless of value, without prior approval.
## Nature of Transactions:
- Gifts, entertainment expenditures, and other non-monetary transactions must not exceed ₹2500 per instance without prior approval.
## Annual Aggregate Limits:
- Individual employees and departments must adhere to an annual aggregate limit of ₹1,00,000 for all sensitive transactions combined.
## dentification and Documentation
- Transaction Identification: Employees must identify whether a transaction with an external stakeholder qualifies as a sensitive transaction based on the definitions provided in Section 4.3.
- Documentation: The employee must document the details of the transaction, including:
- Nature of the transaction (e.g., gift, entertainment, travel expense)
- Value of the transaction
- Purpose of the transaction
- Details of the external stakeholder involved
- Any supporting documents (e.g., receipts, invoices)
- Submit the supporting documents to the immediate supervisor for initial review.
- Approval for Low-Value Transactions
- Initial Review: For transactions valued below ₹3,000, the employee must submit the documented details to their immediate supervisor for initial review.
- Supervisor Approval: The immediate supervisor reviews the transaction details to ensure compliance with company policies and provides approval or disapproval.
- Approval: If approved, the supervisor records the approval and informs the employee.
- Disapproval: If disapproved, the supervisor provides reasons and advises on alternative actions.
## Approval for Medium-Value Transactions
- Department Head Submission: For transactions valued between ₹3,000 and ₹10,000, the employee must submit the documented details to the department head.
- Department Head Review: The department head reviews the transaction details, assesses compliance, and considers the potential impact on the organization.
- Approval: If approved, the department head records the approval and informs the employee.
- Disapproval: If disapproved, the department head provides reasons and suggests alternative actions.
- Approval for High-Value Transactions
- CFO Submission: For transactions valued above ₹10,000, the employee must submit the documented details to the Chief Financial Officer (CFO).
- CFO Review: The CFO reviews the transaction details, ensuring alignment with financial policies, ethical standards, and potential risks.
- Approval: If approved, the CFO records the approval and informs the employee.
